rhs_for_integrator: I0 * exp(-n * sigma * (1 + beta_hard * n * sigma * x) * x) + I0 * f_buildup * (1 - exp(-n * sigma * x)) * exp(-n * sigma_secondary * (1 - gamma_energy * exp(-n * sigma * x)) * x) + I0 * (1 - exp(-n * sigma * x)) * f_buildup_max * (1 - exp(-n * sigma * x)) / (1 + (x / x_sat)**2) * exp(-n * sigma_secondary * (1 - gamma_energy * exp(-n * sigma * x)) * x) + I0 * f_annih * (1 - exp(-n * sigma * x))**2 * exp(-n * sigma * x) * (1 - exp(-x / x_annih)) * exp(-n * sigma_secondary * x)
sanity_expectations: I is strictly positive over the whole region
At x=0, I = I0 = 1 (full beam survives)
I decreases toward 0 as x grows large (attenuation dominates)
At fixed x, I decreases as sigma increases (larger cross section -> more attenuation)
I stays bounded in (0, 1]; primary attenuation term is the dominant contribution, with buildup/secondary terms adding a small positive bump at intermediate thickness
excitation_report: Noise sigma=0.0005 (0.05% of I0=1). Per-term multiples of sigma (rms over the x-sigma region, scaled from the confirmed noise=0.001 run): primary attenuation term ~584x; f_buildup term ~173x; f_buildup_max saturation term ~103x; NEW f_annih secondary-cascade term rms ~6.8x. New-term peak effect (child minus parent) = 14.75*sigma, strongest at x=1.29, sigma=0.81. Every term, including the new annihilation/knock-on term, exceeds 5*sigma. auto_balance converged=true (equivalent solution with I0 scaled instead of noise reduced).
role_corrections: x: axis->independent variable (confirmed): slab thickness, sampled 0-5
sigma: axis->independent variable (confirmed): interaction cross section, varied per phenomenon, sampled 0.5-2
I0: axis->parameter (overridden: I is strictly linear in I0, a pure scale with no shape info; fixed=1, normalized incident beam)
n: axis->parameter (overridden: appears only as the product n*sigma, degenerate with sigma; fixed=1 to resolve degeneracy)
rationale: Static explicit relation I = f(x, sigma; params). Target I is linear on the LHS and fully solvable (analyze_expression: no derivatives, no integral kernels). x (thickness) and sigma (cross section) are the physical sampling axes the experimenters vary, so both are independent variables. I0 is only a linear prefactor (fixed=1) and n is degenerate with sigma inside the n*sigma product (fixed=1); all other symbols are physical constants fixed within hinted/physical magnitudes. Sampling x in [0,5] with n*sigma of order 1 gives exp(-n*sigma*x) spanning ~1 to <0.01, exciting attenuation, buildup, saturation, and the new secondary-cascade term. Noise 0.0005 keeps all four additive terms above 5*sigma; the new f_annih term peaks at ~14.8*sigma near x~1.3.

scenario_text: A beam of particles passes through a slab of absorbing material with a fixed number density of scattering centers. The transmitted intensity decreases with the thickness traversed due to a constant interaction cross section. Experimenters vary the slab thickness and the cross section to measure attenuation. The output is the fraction of the beam that survives passage.
